In the LINE network embedding framework, the authors compare the neighborhood vectors p_u and p_v using the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence. The exact similarity/distance function is

D_{KL}(p_u \| p_v) = \sum_i p_u(i) \log \frac{p_u(i)}{p_v(i)}.

For second-order proximity, they minimize this divergence between the empirical neighborhood distribution of a vertex and the distribution predicted by its embedding.
confidence_reasoning: This is a standard, explicit formula from the LINE paper’s second-order proximity objective, and I am highly confident it is stated correctly.
